propositions: The import-linter job in _optionality.yml performs byte-identical setup to _build-and-test.yml and runs tests that are already collected by the matrix cells, making it redundant and consuming one of 21 concurrent slots against a GitHub Free org cap of 20.

Deleting import-linter opens a gap where future contributors could add pytest markers or move test files, causing optionality tests to drop from the default suite with no alarm, because workflow parity checks only verify wiring strings and job keys, not inner job collection logic.

A durable collection guard test must be added to assert that tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py and tests/unit/test_optional.py collect exactly 9 items under default suite selection, failing if any future marker or file move excludes them.

The three core optionality tests use subprocess isolation, ast.parse analysis, or module eviction fixtures that are not weakened by a shared worker process, so the import-linter dedicated job provides no meaningful import-pollution guard.

The follow-up snapshot rollback risk requires removing stale 'import-linter' context strings from infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json to prevent emergency rollback commands from demanding a check that no longer exists.
